result:
The answer of 120 is very likely wrong, though I could not confirm it by full computation.

The solution's claim that tautological operations cannot improve on the complete-intersection class θ⁵ = 120γ is only asserted, not proved. The "K-theoretic verification" and the Pontryagin coefficient computation are not justified in any way that excludes smaller multiples.

The Fourier–Mukai transform is also not excluded as a source of smaller classes. It sends θ^k/k! to ±θ^{g−k}/(g−k)!, so θ ↦ ±γ for g = 6. But ch(P) for the Poincaré bundle P has denominators, so integrality of the transformed class is not automatic. The true minimal multiple therefore requires a finer argument. As I recall, results on the integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles on very general principally polarized abelian varieties (Beckmann–de Gaay Fortman and others) give a minimal multiple strictly smaller than (g−1)! in this range. I am not certain of the exact value for g = 6.

Because the solution rests on an unproven "no improvement" claim and ignores finer constructions, I do not trust 120.

VERDICT: REJECT
